name: Laser hair-growth cap

lead: A laser hair-growth cap is a wearable helmet-style device with an array of low-power red-light laser diodes or LEDs, worn for around 10 to 30 minutes on a set schedule. Several models hold US FDA clearance as devices for treating androgenetic alopecia, and they are sold as drug-free adjuncts to minoxidil or finasteride.

In looksmaxxing communities the caps are discussed as a hands-off way to slow or partly reverse thinning on the crown and hairline. The clinical literature reports a modest gain in hair density rather than full restoration, which is consistent with the dermatology-society position that the devices can help somewhat but do not return a full head of hair.

paras: The approach is called low-level light therapy or photobiomodulation. Red light at roughly 650 nm is absorbed by chromophores in follicle cells, particularly in mitochondria, and is hypothesised to raise cellular energy output, prolong the growth phase of the hair cycle and reduce follicular inflammation. The exact pathway has not been established, and the optimal wavelength, dose and schedule have not been determined.

Side effects are reported as rare and mild, mostly scalp warmth, dryness or tingling. Pooled analyses of sham-controlled trials report an average density gain, but the trials are small, short and often manufacturer-linked, with substantial heterogeneity. Results are reported to depend on consistent use for months, and benefits fade when use stops. Many lower-priced caps sold online are LED-only products with no clinical data, so FDA clearance is specific to individual models. Studies and guidelines generally place the devices below finasteride or minoxidil in effect when used alone.
